text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the CP segmentation spike — thinking about a minimal handshake between control-plane and tenant egress (private/VPC) so we can preserve source IPs for customer telemetry while still supporting graceful fallback to our relay. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a rollout sketch.

jordi: Curious — when you say preserve source IP, do we mean preserving the tenant's original pod IP all the way to the destination, or just the public egress IP on the customer NAT?

maya: Good call. For most customers we care about the public egress IP (so their firewall rules & third-party allowlists keep working). We also want to avoid hairpin NAT at our edge that would break client IP-based rate limits. We do not need to tunnel L3 pod addresses through us.

akshay: Proposed minimal API: CP -> tenant-egress operator handshake. CP posts a request, operator responds with allowed egress mode and metadata. Something like: 
```json
POST /v1/egress-handshake
{ "tenant_id": "t123", "session_id": "s456", "want_preserve_ip": true }

200 OK
{ "mode": "nat_preserve", "egress_ip": "3.4.5.6", "token": "short-lived-token", "supports_mtls": true }
```
Fields: mode in [nat_preserve, relay, passthrough], egress_ip optional, token short-lived for auth.

jordi: That covers the happy path. How do we validate trust? If CP is in-hosted we need to avoid trusting arbitrary endpoints. mTLS + short-lived certs?

maya: Yes. mTLS mutual auth bound to tenant_id and a short TTL (5m). CP will rotate certs via the same control channel we use for agents. The token in handshake is to avoid exposing long-term creds.

nora: Rollout concerns: some tenants will be on older egress agents that don't implement the new handshake. We should:
- Default to relay when agent doesn't respond 
- Emit a metric to identify tenants that fall back 
- Provide a canary toggle so we can enable handshake per-customer 

sam: Metrics/SLIs to add: 
- cp.egress.handshake.attempts (labels: tenant_id, mode_requested)
- cp.egress.handshake.success (labels: reason:preserved|fallbacked)
- cp.egress.fallback.count (labels: fallback_mode)
- cp.egress.latency_ms (histogram)

Actionable SLO: handshake success rate >= 99% over 5m for dedicated customers; alert if fallback spikes > 0.5%/5m for enterprise.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: staged handshake feature flag (egress-handshake) enabled for org:internal-test yesterday 2024-06-18T16:22Z

akshay: We also need to define a TTL and refresh behavior. My suggestion: token TTL 5m, CP retries handshake every 30s until token obtained, treat no-response within 2m as relay fallback. Also, when mode==nat_preserve, CP should verify that egress_ip matches an allowlist to avoid accidental leak.

jordi: What about TLS termination? If tenant wants us to terminate TLS for performance, that forces relay mode vs passthrough. We should clearly document that nat_preserve implies passthrough L4 and no TLS termination at our relay.

maya: Agree. nat_preserve == L3/4 keepalive; passthrough means we don't inspect. relay means we terminate and forward — higher cost but allows advanced features (observability, dynamic rewrites). We'll gate termination behind explicit tenant consent + enterprise contract.

nora: Config refresh: operator should push a signed capability blob to CP every ~5m; CP caches for up to 10m with a hard fail to relay after cache expiry. Avoid thundering herd by staggering refresh windows.

sam: Observability: add a per-request header we can record when we successfully preserved egress IP: `X-RW-Egress-Mode: nat_preserve` so downstream logs can correlate. Also emit sampling traces for TLS vs non-TLS paths.

maya: Security notes: 
- Handshake audit log in CP with tenant_id, decision, egress_ip, timestamp
- KMS-backed signing for capability blobs
- RBAC: only control-plane role can call /egress-handshake for a tenant

akshay: Cost tradeoff: nat_preserve is cheapest for us but requires customer-managed NAT capacity. Relay imposes egress bandwidth + proxy CPU. We should surface estimated incremental cost when ops enable relay mode in Console.

jordi: Migration plan sketch: 
1) RFC -> implement server side in CP + feature flag (done in staging)
2) implement handshake in new egress-agent (vX) and release canary images to internal-test
3) enable handshake for a small set of low-risk tenants, monitor metrics for 72h
4) Gradually expand; provide customer-facing docs + checkbox in Console to opt into TLS termination (relay)

nora: Edge case: some tenants have split egress (multiple public IPs). Handshake should allow returning a list of egress_ips and an optional `session_affinity_key` so CP can pick the right mapping.

sam: Ops playbook for incidents: 
- If handshake failures spike, flip feature flag to force relay for affected tenants (fast rollback).
- If we detect IP mismatch we should automatically backoff to relay and open a P1 if >5% sessions fail.

maya: Owners & next steps: 
- akshay: write minimal handshake API spec (openapi) + implement server shim
- jordi: auth/mTLS cert rotation design + threat model
- nora: rollout plan + customer docs + console toggle UX
- sam: metrics + alerts + tracing flags
I'll update the RFC with these notes and a reference implementation prototype. Link to follow in the RFC thread. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: noted owners and created issue RW-ops/egress-handshake-2024 for tracking

maya: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the design checkpoint. If anyone sees major gaps call them out here and I'll fold into the spec.
